# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. The manual is mine alone, and so far it holds one row: **when the light is blue, the wire to cut is yellow.** It also tells me the light walks a fixed circle of seven colours, one step per round, and only the colour showing at the instant of the cut matters. If the table's rows march in step with the rounds, this round's light should be blue — but I cannot verify that, because I never see the bomb.

What I can and cannot do: I have no voice and no hands on the bomb. My only channel is gesture, and only the Deaf can see gestures. Crucially, I can *hear* both of them, so the workable loop is: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks questions aloud, and I answer with signs at my next turn. No wire gets cut until that loop has confirmed a shared code — a wrong cut kills all three of us, and no colour word can survive a cold hand-sign unanchored.

So this first packet is a handshake, not an order. I send Deaf: a greeting; a plea for cooperation; the pair 👍👎 to propose that I will answer yes/no questions (the one sign pair that carries its meaning on its face); finger-counts 5+2 = **seven**, the size of the colour circle; and 🤙 — the handshape of the letter "Y" — as a first, testable hint that the word I need them to hold is **yellow**. If Deaf reads even part of this, they can ask aloud "does 👍 mean yes? did 🤙 mean yellow? is the light blue now?" and I will confirm next round. Everything waits on that confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "👍", "👎", "🖐", "✌", "🤙"])
```

Please check the manual for the display, the light and the wire module and tell me exactly which printed details you need to decide. Deaf speaks after me and cannot hear any of us - but Deaf can speak, and their words reach me next round and you immediately. Between Deaf's eyes and your manual I need a complete readout of every colour and marking before I act.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🤝 👍 👎 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐]

Parsing what arrived: Blind has spoken — three wires at fixed positions 1, 2, 3, a display panel, a light panel, and the only act in the whole game is `cut(position)`. Blind cannot feel any printed colour, so **position-to-colour mapping is the entire problem**. And Deaf gestured back: greeting, partnership, echoing my 👍👎 yes/no protocol — then ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐, which I read as *"cut — position 1? position 2? the yellow one? okay? five components"* (display + light + three wires is indeed five). Deaf hears everything, so Deaf already heard Blind's full request for a readout; they're asking me what the manual says the cut should be.

Critical constraints I've traced: I have **no channel to Blind** — only Deaf's spoken relay can carry anything to them. And the light changes **every round**, with the manual counting only the colour *at the cut moment*. Deaf speaks last in the order, so any readout Deaf gives me arrives at my next turn, my answer gestures reach Deaf that same round, Deaf relays, Blind cuts the round after — a two-round lag from first reading to cut. Until my manual table grows beyond one row, I cannot compute the light's future colour, so **no cut yet**. This round I must: (1) hold the cut with 🤚, (2) confirm the protocol with 👍, (3) anchor 🤙 as yellow — the cut colour when the light is blue, (4) put the real question to Deaf: **which position is yellow?** with ☝✌ and a question mark 🤌 aimed at 🫵 them, and (5) remind them of the seven-colour cycle (🖐✌) so they report the light's current colour too, in plain spoken words — colour *names* need no sign code between Deaf's eyes and Deaf's voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "👍", "🫵", "✊", "🤙", "☝", "✌", "🤌", "🖐", "✌", "🤌"])
```

So the relay is exactly: my gestures → Deaf's eyes; Deaf's *voice* → Blind's ears and mine. Deaf is the only bridge to the one monkey who can cut, and so far Deaf has only signed — signs die with me, they never reach Blind. So this packet: 👏👏 — a clap is a *sound*; make sound, speak, every round (repeated = always). Then 🖐 with ☝✌🤟 = one-two-three: speak all five printed things — display, light, wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Then 👎✊ = do not cut yet. Then 🤙🤌🫵 = "yellow — which position? you tell me." Then 🖐✌👏🤌 = "the seven — speak it — which colour now?" If Deaf starts voicing the readout, I hear it directly, check it against my table, and sign back the cut position for Deaf to voice to Blind.
